question: Which of the following metals has the lowest melting point?
solution:
The correct answer is __Mercury**(Hg)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mercury__ is a unique metal that remains in liquid form at room temperature.
 
• Its melting point is -38.83°C, which is lower than other metals like Lead, Iron, or Gold.
 
• Mercury is used in thermometers, barometers, and various scientific instruments.
 
• Due to its liquid state at room temperature, it has extensive applications in electronics and chemical industries.
 
• Mercury is highly toxic and requires careful handling and disposal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Lead:**

 
 
• The melting point of Lead is 327.5°C.
 
• It is used in batteries, radiation shielding, and construction materials.
 
 
 
• **Iron:**
 
 
• Iron has a melting point of 1538°C.
 
• It is one of the most commonly used metals in construction, tools, and machinery.
 
 
 
• **Gold:**
 
 
• Gold melts at 1064°C.
 
• It is widely used in jewelry, electronics, and as a valuable investment asset.
